subject: Order Form: confidentiality breach trigger & remediation (liability cap clarification)
body:
From: Marci Delores <marci@stellarsystems.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Liability carve-out language for trade-secret incidents

Hi Jonas / Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We like to move forward but legal is flagging the Order Form liability section. Their ask: an explicit carve-out to the liability cap for breaches involving Stellars trade secrets and confidential data where misappropriation is found. They like the carve-out to be uncapped for direct damages and to permit immediate preservation/forensics and remedial costs.

Can Redwood accept language along these lines (we attached a redline):
- Carve-out applies where a court or independent forensic report finds willful misappropriation or intentional exfiltration of trade secrets;
- Breaching party bears preservation/forensics costs and reasonable remediation;
- Unlimited liability for direct damages caused by such willful conduct;
- No change to consequential damages exclusion.

They also like a 30-day preservation window and a requirement to engage an independent forensic vendor if requested. Attaching their proposed redline (stellarsystems_redline_v1.docx).

Appreciate a quick read — our procurement timeline is ~two weeks.

Best,
Marci
Director, Procurement
Stellar Systems
Attachments: stellarsystems_redline_v1.docx

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Liability carve-out language for trade-secret incidents

Laura / Rafael, looping you in. Marci sent Stellar's procurement redline (attached). Quick thoughts:
- We should push back on "uncapped for direct damages" across the board. Agree we need a narrow trigger for unlimited exposure only for: (i) judicial finding of willful misappropriation OR (ii) a high-confidence independent forensic report showing deliberate exfiltration attributable to Redwood systems/agents.
- Require immediate notice + preservation; require Stellar to provide a specific remediation plan and allowances for Redwood to investigate and cure before full indemnity kicks in.
- Forensics: suggest a fixed-cost advance for triage and Redwood reserves the right to appoint an independent vendor.

Can legal draft language that: limits the carve-out to willful misappropriation, ties unlimited liability to direct damages only (excluding consequential), requires notice and preservation, and includes a defined path for forensic engagement/cost allocation.

Thanks,
Jonas
Head of Sales (West)
Redwood Inference
Attachment: internal_ask.docx

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Marci Delores <marci@stellarsystems.com>, Nora Lee <nora.lee@carterlee.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 22:30:00 +00:00
Subject: RE: Liability carve-out language for trade-secret incidents (redline attached)

Jonas / Laura / Marci / Nora —

Thanks for the clear note and the redline. I reviewed the proposed language and attached a concise counter-redline (redwood_legal_commentary.pdf) with the following summary:

1) Trigger. Redwood can accept a narrow carve-out limited to: (a) a final judicial determination of willful misappropriation, or (b) a forensic report from an agreed independent vendor (selected jointly or via a neutral panel) that identifies intentional exfiltration by an individual acting with intent to steal trade secrets. The forensic path must include an appeals/cure window (we recommended 30 days) and an evidentiary threshold (high confidence).

2) Scope of unlimited liability. We will accept uncapped liability only for direct, provable damages caused by the willful conduct defined above. We will expressly exclude consequential, incidental, punitive, and speculative damages from the unlimited carve-out.

3) Forensics & preservation. Redwood commits to timely acknowledgement of suspected incidents (48 hours), immediate preservation steps, and cooperation with Stellar's forensic vendor. Costs for an initial triage are to be split proportionally: if the forensic report determines no willful misappropriation, Redwood may seek reimbursement of triage costs; if willful misappropriation is confirmed, the breaching party bears forensic and remediation costs plus direct damages.

4) Procedural safeguards. Redwood requests notice and an opportunity to investigate/remediate before indemnity obligations shift into effect; urgent relief (injunctive) remains available to Stellar.

If that outline is acceptable, I propose we forward the redline and ask Stellars counsel to confirm the independent-forensic vendor selection mechanics and the appeals/cure window.

Redwood attachment: redwood_legal_commentary.pdf

Regards,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

-----Forwarded message attached-----

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Marci Delores <marci@stellarsystems.com>, Nora Lee <nora.lee@carterlee.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Liability carve-out language for trade-secret incidents (accept in principle)

Marci / Nora,

Thanks for the patience while we reviewed. We can accept a narrowly tailored carve-out with the following binding points (redlined language attached via DocuSign link):

- Trigger definition: carve-out limited to (i) final judicial adjudication of willful misappropriation, or (ii) a high-confidence independent forensic report identifying intentional exfiltration attributable to Redwood systems or personnel.
- Remedies: unlimited liability is limited to direct, provable damages caused by the willful act; consequential and indirect damages remain excluded.
- Forensics & costs: Redwood will acknowledge suspected incidents within 48 hours and take preservation steps. The initial triage cost will be split 50/50; if the forensic report confirms willful misappropriation, the breaching party shall bear forensic and remediation costs and direct damages. If the report does not confirm willful misappropriation, Redwood may seek reimbursement of triage costs.
- Procedural: Stellar must provide notice and a reasonable remediation window (we propose 30 days) before indemnity transfers, except in cases where injunctive relief is necessary. Vendor selection procedure for the independent forensic firm: joint selection, or arbitration panel if parties cannot agree.

Please confirm acceptance of the attached redline or propose modifications. When we have mutual agreement, I like to close the Order Form via DocuSign to meet Stellars procurement timetable.

DocuSign order form link: https://docusign.com/REDACTED/ORDERFORM/DEAL-4321

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales (West) | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_legal_commentary.pdf
